correctness.rationale: Equal length and equal total standard weight force every Parikh difference to lie on the one-dimensional lattice generated by \((1,-2,1)\). The shared one-letter maximum forces the lower-c word to contain at least one c, yielding the sharp count bound for even lengths. The only possible larger odd-length endpoint would compare a word with counts \((0,2r,1)\) to one with counts \((r,0,r+1)\); their length-two factor-weight maxima cannot agree because the former has maximum 5 while the latter can only have maximum 4 or 6. Explicit even and odd witness families have factor-weight signatures computed in closed form and their stated prefix-normal representatives realize the bound. The finite verifier independently exhausts all ternary words through length 9.
